E: A work log bearing traces of practice for document forgery can be used, when public and private interests are balanced, as evidence of guilt to prove the defendant's litigation fraud, but if that work log was stolen by a third party and the victim of the litigation fraud acquired it by paying consideration, it cannot be used as evidence of guilt.
label: A

question: Which of the following statements concerning the admissibility of documentary hearsay evidence is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: If a witness, even after the criminal judgment related to himself had become final and binding, refused without justifiable reason to testify in court, so that the Defendant was unable to cross-examine him, then even if the Defendant caused the witness’s refusal to testify, a document recording that witness’s statement at the investigative agency does not fall under Article 314 of the Criminal Procedure Act’s “where a statement cannot be made due to any other similar reason,” and thus has no evidentiary admissibility.
B: The phrase “an interrogation protocol of a suspect prepared by a prosecutor” in Article 312(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act means not only an interrogation protocol of the Defendant in question, but also an interrogation protocol prepared by a prosecutor with respect to another Defendant or suspect who is in a co-offender relationship with the Defendant in question, and “co-offender” in this context includes a counterpart offender.
C: A protocol recording the contents of an examination of a suspect or reference person who became the Defendant, conducted by a tax official in charge of tax offense investigations, constitutes a statement prepared by a Defendant or a person other than the Defendant, or a document recording such statement, and therefore its admissibility as evidence must be determined pursuant to Article 313 of the Criminal Procedure Act.
D: In an insurance fraud case, a “reply to a request for review of whether inpatient medical treatment was appropriate, etc., from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service,” which states the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service’s opinion on the appropriateness of inpatient medical treatment based on the materials sent to it by the investigative agency, does not constitute a document continuously and mechanically recording the details of office processing, and therefore does not fall under “a document prepared under particularly trustworthy circumstances” under Article 315(3) of the Criminal Procedure Act.
E: A protocol in which a hearsay statement is recorded is admissible as evidence when it satisfies the requirements of Article 312 or Article 314 of the Criminal Procedure Act and the requirements of Article 316 of the Criminal Procedure Act.
label: A

question: Which of the following statements concerning appeals is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: Even though defense counsel indicated an intention to question the Defendant at the appellate trial, the presiding judge’s measure of not allowing defense counsel to question the Defendant at all constitutes a violation of the laws governing litigation procedure and falls under a ground for final appeal.
B: In a case in which only the Defendant appealed, even if the appellate court found some of the criminal facts recognized by the court of first instance to be not guilty and nevertheless imposed on the Defendant the same sentence as the court of first instance, this does not violate the principle prohibiting disadvantageous modification.
C: Where the Defendant did not appeal the first-instance judgment in which guilt was affirmed, or appealed only on the ground of improper sentence, and the prosecutor also appealed only on the ground of improper sentence, and the appellate court accepted the prosecutor’s appeal, reversed the first-instance judgment, and imposed a higher sentence than that judgment, the Defendant cannot assert new grounds such as factual error or violation of laws and regulations as grounds for final appeal.
D: Where, with respect to an appellate judgment that acquitted the Defendant of some of the concurrent crimes and convicted the Defendant of some of the concurrent crimes, only the prosecutor filed a final appeal as to the acquittal portion, when reversing it in the final appeal, only the acquittal portion must be reversed.
E: Where, with respect to the first-instance judgment, the Defendant filed a leapfrog appeal and the prosecutor filed an appeal, and these were concurrent, the Defendant’s leapfrog appeal loses its effect; therefore, even if the Defendant’s leapfrog appeal satisfied all the lawful requirements as an appeal, such as compliance with the appeal period, and even if the Defendant had an intention to challenge the first-instance judgment in the appellate trial, effect as an appeal cannot be given to the Defendant’s leapfrog appeal.
label: E

question: Which of the following statements concerning seizure and search are incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) If the person subject to seizure expressly indicated to the investigative agency that he would not participate in the execution of the seizure/search warrant, then, except in special circumstances, it is permissible not to separately guarantee his defense counsel an opportunity to participate in the execution of the seizure/search warrant. (b) If, after the investigative agency has selectively seized information related to the alleged crime and is retaining the remaining information unrelated thereto without deleting, discarding, or returning it, then, as to the portion unrelated to the alleged crime, it has unlawfully seized and searched electronic information beyond the scope of electronic information subject to seizure without a warrant, and such illegality cannot be deemed cured merely because a seizure/search warrant was later issued by a court or because the defendant or defense counsel consented to its use as evidence. (c) The term "an information storage medium belonging to the suspect's ownership or management," for which the right of participation should be guaranteed not only to the person subject to seizure who voluntarily submitted the information storage medium but also to a suspect who is not the voluntary submitter, means a case in which the suspect, at the time of the seizure/search or up to a temporally proximate time, actually controlled and managed the information storage medium and possessed and exercised exclusive authority to manage and dispose of all electronic information within that information storage medium, and did not otherwise transfer or relinquish it to a third party according to his own intent, so that the suspect can be evaluated as the substantive person subject to seizure with respect to the electronic information stored in that information storage medium. (d) Whether a person qualifies as the substantive person subject to seizure must be determined on the basis of the externally and objectively recognizable factual condition at the time of the seizure/search; thus, if the suspect or any other third party had, in the past, been involved in the use of that information storage medium or the creation or use of individual electronic information, or if they are the data subject identified by electronic information created in the course thereof, then they must be treated as the party substantively subjected to seizure and search. (e) If, while voluntarily submitting a mobile phone, the suspect voluntarily provided the investigative agency with the ID and password for accessing cloud services or the like, with the intent of submitting to the investigative agency electronic information stored not in the mobile phone but in remote locations managed by a third party such as the cloud, then the electronic information stored in the cloud or the like may be regarded as having been voluntarily submitted.
label: A

question: Which of the following explanations concerning jurisdiction is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: With respect to a first-instance criminal case, the main office of a district court and a branch office of a district court are separate courts under procedural law and stand in an equal relationship, each sharing a specified territorial jurisdiction area; therefore, unless there are special circumstances from which it may be concluded that first-instance territorial jurisdiction is recognized for the main office of a district court, it cannot be said that first-instance territorial jurisdiction is naturally recognized for the main office of a district court merely because first-instance territorial jurisdiction is recognized for a branch office of a district court.
B: When an appellate case concerning a defendant case within the jurisdiction of a single judge is pending before a panel of a branch office of a district court, the court with jurisdiction over a medical treatment and custody case requested by the time of the close of oral argument is the High Court, and the court with jurisdiction over the defendant case also becomes the High Court following the jurisdiction over the medical treatment and custody case; and if such a medical treatment and custody case is requested to a branch office of a district court and assigned to the panel in charge of the appeal of the defendant case, that panel must transfer both the medical treatment and custody case and the defendant case to the High Court.
C: Where a case within the jurisdiction of a panel is changed into a case within the jurisdiction of a single judge by amendment of the indictment, the panel must proceed to adjudicate the substance of the case and cannot reassign the case to a single judge.
D: Territorial jurisdiction is sufficient if it exists at the time of institution of prosecution, and in the event of a jurisdictional violation, records of the trial proceedings, such as a trial record and a witness examination record, prepared in the trial proceedings of the court that rendered a judgment of jurisdictional violation may be used as evidence if prosecution is instituted again with respect to the relevant case.
E: When the same case is pending before multiple courts having the same subject-matter jurisdiction, in principle the court that first received the indictment shall try the case, and in this case the court that will not conduct a trial due to concurrent jurisdiction shall render a judgment dismissing the indictment.
label: E

question: Which of the following statements concerning a request for adjudication is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: If a request for adjudication is filed, the running of the Statute of Limitations for prosecution is suspended until the adjudication decision becomes final and conclusive, and the prosecutor who instituted the prosecution by the court’s decision to institute prosecution may amend the indictment so long as the identity of the charges is recognized, but may not withdraw the prosecution.
B: A request for adjudication may be withdrawn until the court renders its decision, and the effect of such withdrawal does not extend to other joint persons entitled to request.
C: Where, after the period for filing a request for adjudication has elapsed, a supplementary brief for request for adjudication is submitted and facts of accusation not originally subject to the request for adjudication are added as the subject of the request for adjudication, the request for adjudication as to the portion added in that supplementary brief is contrary to the legal form and thus unlawful.
D: With respect to a case for which a decision dismissing a request for adjudication has become final and conclusive, prosecution is barred except where other important evidence is discovered; here, a “case for which a decision dismissing a request for adjudication has become final and conclusive” means only a case that became the subject of a decision dismissing the request for adjudication after the court in charge of the request for adjudication actually conducted review and made a determination on the possibility and necessity of instituting prosecution.
E: If a complainant in prison submitted a request for adjudication to the warden of the prison, or to a person acting on behalf of the warden’s duties, within the period for filing a request for adjudication, then even if that request for adjudication did not reach the chief prosecutor of the district prosecutor’s office, or the chief of the branch office, to which the prosecutor who rendered the non-prosecution disposition belongs, within the above period, it shall be deemed to have been lawfully submitted.
label: E

question: Which of the following statements concerning special criminal procedures are all correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) Once the chief of a police station has issued a notice disposition for an offense subject to a notice disposition, since the offender who pays the fine in accordance with the notice disposition is afforded an opportunity to be exempted from criminal prosecution and criminal punishment, until the fine payment period specified in the notice disposition expires, the chief of a police station, as a matter of principle, may not request a summary trial, and the prosecutor may not institute a prosecution for the same offense subject to a notice disposition. (b) In summary trial proceedings, a suspect interrogation protocol prepared by a judicial police officer in accordance with lawful procedure and method is admissible as evidence even if the defendant, who had been the suspect, does not admit its contents; corroborating evidence for a confession is not required, but the confession exclusionary rule still applies. (c) A summary order becomes effective upon service of the written judgment on the defendant, and even where defense counsel exists, it is not necessarily required that a copy of the summary order be served on defense counsel; therefore, the period for filing a formal trial request must be calculated from the date of notice of the summary order to the defendant. (d) The principle of prohibition against increasing the type of punishment prescribed in Article 457-2(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act applies unchanged, even in a case where a case for which only the defendant requested a formal trial and another case are jointly tried and thereafter punished as concurrent offenses, and the same applies to an appeal from a first-instance judgment that imposed a fine in a case where only the defendant requested a formal trial. (e) Where multiple acts corresponding to the same offense name are continuously committed over a certain period under a single and continuous intent, and the protected legal interest harmed is also the same, so that the offenses are in the relationship of a comprehensive single offense, if a summary order has become final and conclusive with respect to part of such offenses, the res judicata of the summary order extends, based on the time of issuance of the summary order, not only to offenses that constitute part of the comprehensive single offense committed before that time, but also to other offenses in the relationship of ideal concurrence with them.
label: E

question: Which of the following statements concerning preservation of evidence under Article 184 of the Criminal Procedure Act (A) and a petition for witness examination under Article 221-2 (B) is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: A may not be petitioned before the suspect or defendant has been formally booked in a criminal case.
B: A matter that constitutes suspect interrogation cannot be petitioned by the A method, and even if the suspect is interrogated by the A method and the contents of that interrogation include a statement concerning another accomplice, if that accomplice had not been formally booked at the time of the interrogation, the effect of preservation of evidence concerning that accomplice cannot be recognized.
C: When a judge conducts witness examination under the A procedure, the prosecutor, suspect, or defense counsel must be notified in advance of the date and place of the witness examination and given an opportunity to participate in the witness examination; however, even if no opportunity to participate was given, if the defendant and defense counsel agreed that the witness examination record may be used as evidence and, without any special objection, it was lawfully subjected to evidentiary examination, the said witness examination record is admissible.
D: Even where a reference person who made a voluntary statement to a prosecutor or judicial police officer is likely to make a statement at the trial date different from the prior statement, and where that statement is recognized as indispensable to proving the offense, the prosecutor may petition a judge for examination of that person as a witness pursuant to the B procedure only before the first trial date.
E: A witness examination record conducted under the procedures of A and B is admissible pursuant to Article 311 of the Criminal Procedure Act.
label: D

question: A, while preparing for a divorce action due to discord with her husband A, who had a severe drinking habit and pathological jealousy, asked B, A’s driver, to kill A. At A’s request, B strangled and killed A, who was drunk and asleep. The prosecutor indicted B for murder and A for instigating murder, and the court is conducting a joint trial of A and B. Which of the following statements are incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) If A, in an interrogation of a suspect by a judicial police officer, admitted the instigation, but denies it in court, the suspect interrogation record prepared by the judicial police officer concerning A, in which A denied the contents, may be used as rebuttal evidence to impeach A’s in-court testimony, insofar as voluntariness is recognized. (b) If W, B’s friend, appears in court and testifies that B told him, “I killed A,” W’s testimony cannot be used as evidence of B’s guilt so long as B, the original declarant, is appearing in court. (c) If both A and B are confessing to the charged facts, but there is no other evidence corroborating the confessions, A and B must be acquitted. (d) If A confesses in court to instigating the murder of A, A’s statement may be used as evidence of B’s guilt. (e) Even if the court of first instance, in sentencing A, did not specify the fact that B strangled and killed A, if there are special circumstances showing that A’s right of defense or A’s counsel’s right of defense was not essentially infringed, it is not a violation of law that affected the judgment.
label: C

question: Which of the following statements concerning trial proceedings are correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) If the defendant failed to appear on the first trial date in the appellate instance, appeared on the second trial date, but again failed to appear on the third trial date, and the court proceeded with the trial proceedings in the presence only of the defendant's defense counsel and the prosecutor, closed the arguments, and then pronounced a judgment dismissing the defendant's appeal on the fourth trial date, this is lawful as a measure under Article 365 of the Criminal Procedure Act. (b) In first-instance trial proceedings, if the defendant's whereabouts cannot be ascertained for six months from the receipt of a report of failure of service on the defendant, the case may be tried without the defendant's statement in accordance with the Supreme Court Rules; however, in cases punishable by death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment or penal detention for a term exceeding 10 years, the case may not be tried without the defendant's statement. (c) The opportunity to state the final opinion need only be given to the defendant or defense counsel; therefore, even if the presiding judge, immediately after defense counsel's final argument, designated and notified the date for pronouncement of judgment, thereby closing the arguments and pronouncing judgment without giving the defendant an opportunity to state a final opinion, this is an act of discretion within the scope of the presiding judge's power to direct the proceedings and cannot be regarded as a violation of the law in the procedural proceedings. (d) Whether to reopen closed arguments is, in principle, a matter within the court's discretion; however, if the appellate court did not grant a motion for reopening of arguments filed by defense counsel appointed after the close of arguments, this corresponds to a case in which there is illegality due to incomplete hearing. (e) Whether to admit an evidentiary application is within the court's discretion, so with respect to the court's evidentiary decision neither an ordinary appeal nor an immediate appeal may be taken; rather, an objection may be raised only when the evidentiary decision violates statutes and regulations, and it may also be used as a ground for appeal only when, as a result, there has been a mistaken finding of facts affecting the judgment.
label: B

question: Which of the following statements concerning the institution of public prosecution and amendment of the indictment is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: Even if the prosecution was instituted without specifying the defendant, if the defendant and defense counsel did not raise an objection and proceeded with the trial, the defect in the prosecution is cured.
B: Even where, because the time, place, means, and object of the offense differ among the criminal facts, they are recognized as multiple criminal facts, those multiple criminal facts may be pleaded alternatively or in the alternative.
C: In the case of a comprehensive single offense, in determining whether to grant leave to amend the indictment, rather than examining, for each individual count constituting the comprehensive single offense, whether it is identical to the former one, the focus should be on whether the amended facts, viewed as a whole, fall within the category of a comprehensive single offense; that is, whether they may be regarded as a case in which the same kind of offense is repeatedly committed under a single and continuous criminal intent and the protected legal interest harmed is also the same.
D: Even where, as a result of an amendment to the indictment, the case no longer qualifies as a case subject to a citizen participation trial, the court must continue the citizen participation trial; however, the court may decide to have the case tried by the collegiate division of the main branch of the District Court without a citizen participation trial, and no appeal lies against such decision.
E: Even if, without the intent and ability to perform repayment, the defendant was prosecuted for having defrauded money from the victim, if it is recognized, without going through the procedure for amendment of the indictment, as the fact that the defendant caused the victim to be introduced to a third party, borrowed the same amount of money, and thereby obtained a property benefit by causing the victim to assume a surety obligation therefor, there can be no illegality.
label: A

question: Entertainer A, around 08:00 on 2023. 3. 9., while driving his passenger car, which was covered by comprehensive automobile insurance, on a highway, struck the curb on the left side of the road, and as a result of the impact, sustained an injury requiring six weeks of treatment himself and caused an injury requiring eight weeks of treatment to B, who was in the front passenger seat and was in a de facto marital relationship with him. A and B got out of the passenger car immediately after the accident but soon lost consciousness, and were transported to a hospital in that state. When B regained consciousness, B, out of concern that A’s entertainment activities might be affected, made a false statement to Police Officer P that B had been driving the above passenger car and caused the traffic accident. Which of the following statements regarding this is correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: Although P sought to investigate whether B, who had been found near the driver’s seat and transported to the hospital, had driven under the influence, when B did not regain consciousness, and P received, by voluntary submission, from Nurse A a portion of the blood that A had drawn from B for treatment purposes and seized it without a warrant, the seizure procedure violates due process.
B: B was indicted for the crime of violation of the Road Traffic Act (driving under the influence) and the crime of violation of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (injury), and at the first trial date B and B’s counsel objected to the reply to the request for blood examination as evidence; however, if, at the third trial date, while B was absent, B’s counsel consented to its being used as evidence, then the above consent to evidence is effective.
C: After B received a final judgment of conviction for the crime of violation of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (injury), and then broke up with A, if B petitions for a retrial by submitting as evidence a mobile phone photograph of A driving at the time of the above traffic accident, which B had concealed, this falls under the “when clear evidence establishing innocence has been newly discovered” clause in Article 420, item 5, of the Criminal Procedure Act.
D: Even if A cannot be prosecuted for the crime of violation of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (injury) because the above passenger car was covered by comprehensive automobile insurance, B’s act of helping A escape may constitute the crime of harboring a criminal.
E: Even if B’s act of making a false statement to P constitutes the crime of harboring a criminal, B is not punishable because, at the time of the offense, B was in a de facto marital relationship with A.
label: D

question: Party A and A are brothers who do not live together, and A went missing. In around January 2023, Party A, as the court-appointed absentee property administrator for A, received KRW 700 million in expropriation compensation deposited in favor of A. Thereafter, in around March 2023, the court changed the absentee property administrator for A from Party A to B. Nevertheless, Party A neither informed B of the existence of the deposited money nor handed it over. After B learned of these facts in around May 2023, B obtained permission from the court concerning the exercise of the right to file a complaint in around June 2023 and then immediately filed a complaint with the investigative agency against Party A for the offense of violation of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Economic Crimes (Breach of Trust) concerning these facts. Which of the following statements are incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) While Party A, B, and Party A's older sister C were gathered together and talking, B recorded the conversation among the three persons using the voice-recording function of his mobile phone for the purpose of collecting evidence, and such recording act falls under Article 16(1) of the Protection of Communications Secrets Act and is unlawful. (b) B, as the absentee property administrator for A, having obtained permission from the court concerning the exercise of the right to file a complaint regarding criminal acts against A's property, which was the object of administration, qualifies as a lawful person entitled to file a complaint as A's legal representative. (c) After Judicial Police Officer P, having obtained an arrest warrant for Party A for the offense of violation of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Economic Crimes (Breach of Trust), discovered Party A, who had parked a vehicle in the parking lot in front of his house, and arrested Party A pursuant to the arrest warrant while searching Party A's vehicle, such act is lawful under Article 216(1) No. 2 of the Criminal Procedure Act. (d) If Party A injured Judicial Police Officer P by colliding with him with Party A's vehicle during the arrest process described in item (c), then the offense of special obstruction of the execution of official duties causing injury and the offense of special injury are established against Party A, and the two offenses are in a relation of ideal concurrence. (e) If Party A were A's non-cohabiting son and B's complaint had been filed on December 20, 2023, then the court must, with respect to Party A's offense of violation of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Economic Crimes (Breach of Trust), render a judgment dismissing the public prosecution pursuant to Article 327(2) of the Criminal Procedure Act.
label: C

question: A owned building X on land owned by B, but after losing a lawsuit for removal of the building filed by B, and after X was demolished, A newly constructed building Y on the said land. B threw more than 30 eggs at the wall of building Y, causing A to incur cleaning expenses of approximately KRW 500,000 to remove the traces of the eggs remaining on building Y. In response to B's above act, A placed a reinforced concrete structure tightly in front of B's vehicle parked near building Y and an excavator crusher tightly behind it, thereby preventing B from operating the vehicle for approximately 17 hours. Meanwhile, B, angry, used red paint to write graffiti on A's excavator crusher: \"The owner of the illegal building, get out.\" A summary order imposing a fine of KRW 1,000,000 was issued with respect to this criminal act. Which of the following statements concerning this is incorrect? ((If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) A's act of constructing building Y without authorization infringed the utility of B's land itself and constitutes the offense of damaging property. (b) B's act of throwing more than 30 eggs at the wall of building Y infringed the utility of that building and constitutes the offense of damaging property. (c) A's act of rendering B's vehicle incapable of being operated for 17 hours infringed the vehicle's inherent utility and constitutes the offense of damaging property. (d) If B, in objection to the above summary order, requested a formal trial without retaining counsel and thereafter failed to appear on two consecutive occasions, the court may conduct evidentiary examination without B's appearance, and in this case B's consent to evidence is deemed pursuant to Article 318(2) of the Criminal Procedure Act. (e) If B, as in item (d) above, after consent to evidence was deemed in the formal trial and evidentiary examination was completed, was sentenced to a fine of KRW 1,000,000 and appealed, and if B appeared in the appellate trial and expressed an intention to withdraw or revoke the consent to evidence, the effect of the consent to evidence is lost because the deemed consent to evidence at the first instance was made regardless of B's true intention.
label: C

question: A public official, A, for the purpose of concealing the fact that his wife, B, had violated the Building Act, recorded in the official document known as the completion inspection report the statement, “The completion inspection was conducted based on the settlement design document,” even though he had not checked the settlement design document. When A was indicted for the above act and B was requested as a witness, A instigated B to commit perjury, and B then gave false testimony. Which of the following statements is correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: In addition to the crime of making a false official document, the crime of dereliction of duty is also established against A, and the two are in a relation of ideal concurrence.
B: If the contents of the completion inspection report prepared by A objectively correspond to the completion status at the construction site, the crime of making a false official document is not established against A.
C: Because A's act of instigating B to commit perjury, like the act of making a false statement concerning his own criminal case, falls within A's exercise of the right of defense, A cannot be punished for the crime of subornation of perjury.
D: If, during B's witness examination, the prosecutor used leading questions even though B did not show hostility or antipathy toward the prosecutor's direct examination, and if A stated at the next trial date regarding the above witness examination record that there were no points to be changed or objected to, then the defect in the direct examination conducted by leading questions is cured.
E: If the crime of perjury is established for B's false testimony, then even after the criminal trial against A has become final and binding, when B voluntarily reports the perjury, the punishment shall be mitigated or remitted.
label: D

question: A, while residing with his disabled mother A and having lawfully obtained and used a motor vehicle placard for persons with disabilities (for a caregiver), parked his passenger car in a place other than an exclusive parking space for persons with disabilities in an apartment parking lot with the placard still displayed on his passenger car, notwithstanding that, because A’s address differed from his, the “motor vehicle placard for persons with disabilities bearing a parking placard for an exclusive parking space for persons with disabilities” had become ineffective, and was caught in the act. Which of the following statements are incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) Because the crime of unlawful use of an official document is a concrete danger offense, the subject, object, and manner of the offense should be interpreted as strictly as possible so that the scope of punishment is limited within a reasonable range. (b) Even if A did not park the passenger car in an exclusive parking space for persons with disabilities, because A displayed on the passenger car a motor vehicle placard for persons with disabilities for which A had no authority to use, thereby outwardly indicating it as though it were a vehicle used by a person with disabilities, this constitutes unlawful use of a motor vehicle placard for persons with disabilities. (c) If Judge R issued a summary order against A for the crime of unlawful use of an official document, and after being served with it, A submitted to the court, on behalf of A, a request for formal trial bearing only A’s name and lacking a seal or signature, but a court official accepted it without requesting correction, the court cannot render a dismissal decision with respect to the above request for formal trial. (d) If apartment resident B, having been summoned as a witness in A’s formal trial, failed to appear on the ground that B was due to give birth, the statement protocol prepared by a judicial police officer concerning B, to which A did not consent to its use as evidence, cannot have evidentiary admissibility recognized under Article 314 of the Criminal Procedure Act. (e) If Judge R, who issued the summary order, participated in the appellate trial proceedings of the formal trial against A up to the second hearing date but was replaced at the third hearing and did not participate in that judgment, it cannot be said that the judge who participated in the prior trial participated in the trial of the relevant case for which a challenge was filed.
label: A

question: A, a public official with authority to grant building permits, received 20,000,000 won in bribes from C, a building contractor, in connection with a building permit for a building, under the aid and abetment of B, the person in charge of practical affairs. Thereafter, A gave B 2,000,000 won out of the 20,000,000 won as a gratuity, spent 4,000,000 won as necessary expenses for the building permit, and deposited the remaining 14,000,000 won in a bank. When the building permit was later refused, C demanded the return of the entire amount of the bribe he had given to A. A withdrew the 14,000,000 won that had been deposited, on the grounds that he had given 2,000,000 won to B as a gratuity and spent 4,000,000 won as expenses, and returned only that money to C. Which of the following statements concerning this is correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: The 2,000,000 won gratuity that A gave to B cannot be collected from A.
B: Since the 4,000,000 won in necessary expenses that A expended in connection with the building permit cannot be regarded as having been actually acquired by A, it cannot be collected from A.
C: The 14,000,000 won that A returned to C cannot be collected from C.
D: If C is indicted for the offense of bribery-giving and a final conviction is rendered, the statute of limitations for prosecution for A's offense of acceptance of bribes is suspended from the time the above criminal case against C is indicted until the time it becomes final.
E: If B leaves for the United States for the purpose of evading punishment for aiding and abetting the offense of acceptance of bribes, the statute of limitations for prosecution for A, a co-offender, for the offense of acceptance of bribes is also suspended during B's period of flight.
label: C

question: A sold to the voice-phishing scammer B, on 2023. 2. 12., for KRW 1,000,000, a deposit passbook with no balance for a deposit account opened in his own name at X Bank, one debit card linked to the said account, and one OTP card, without knowing that they would be used in a fraud offense. Thereafter, on 2023. 2. 13., B called A and, while impersonating a prosecutor, said, “If you transfer the money to A, who is a financial law expert, I will verify any criminal connection and then return it,” and A, having been deceived thereby, transferred KRW 10,000,000 to the said account around 11:20 on 2023. 2. 14.; and A, around 11:50 on the same day, used the debit card linked to the said account, which he had separately made and had in his possession, and arbitrarily withdrew KRW 3,000,000 of that amount. Regarding this, the prosecutor filed an indictment on the ground that A, by arbitrarily withdrawing KRW 3,000,000 from the fraud proceeds, embezzled B's property primarily and A's property alternatively. However, part of the page seal had been affixed to the reverse side of page 1 of the indictment, but the remaining page seal had not been affixed to the front side of page 2, and there was no page seal from the reverse side of page 2 to the last page. Which of the following statements concerning this is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: After A deposited KRW 10,000,000 into the account in the name of A, A is in the position of holding the said KRW 10,000,000 for the benefit of A.
B: A's act of arbitrarily withdrawing KRW 3,000,000 from the fraud proceeds constitutes the crime of embezzlement against B.
C: If A were an accomplice to B's fraud offense, then the act of arbitrarily withdrawing KRW 3,000,000 from the fraud proceeds does not constitute the crime of embezzlement against A.
D: Even if the indictment lacks the prosecutor's page seal, so long as the form and content of the indictment are recognized as being continuous and its identity is recognized, and it is recognized as having been prepared by the same prosecutor, the indictment cannot be regarded as a document without legal effect.
E: If, in the appellate trial concerning A, a judgment of not guilty is rendered on all counts of the indictment and the prosecutor files an appeal therefrom, then if the alternative count part must be reversed in the Supreme Court trial, the principal count part, which stands in the relationship of the same entity with it, also inevitably must be reversed together.
label: B

question: Which of the following statements concerning the following case is correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) The Chief of the Tax Office imposed a tax disposition on A, who constitutes a secondary taxpayer under the Framework Act on National Taxes, with respect to B Corporation’s delinquent national taxes (hereinafter referred to as “the tax disposition at issue”). The filing period for an administrative lawsuit to assert the illegality of the tax disposition at issue has elapsed. However, one year later, the Constitutional Court, in a constitutional complaint case filed by B, decided that the provision of the Framework Act on National Taxes that served as the basis for the tax disposition at issue was unconstitutional (hereinafter referred to as “the unconstitutional decision at issue”). The Chief of the Tax Office attached the deposit claim in A’s name, on the basis of the National Tax Collection Act, which was validly in force at the time pursuant to the tax disposition at issue, in order to collect the delinquent amount and deficiency amount (including additional tax) that A had been in arrears with.
A: Since the provision of the Framework Act on National Taxes that served as the basis for the tax disposition at issue was declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court, the tax disposition at issue is a disposition lacking legal basis and is therefore void ab initio; accordingly, although the filing period has elapsed, bringing an administrative lawsuit seeking confirmation of its nullity is lawful.
B: The statutory provision that was the subject of the unconstitutional decision is the basis of the tax disposition at issue, and even if the retroactive effect of the unconstitutional decision is recognized, there is no risk of undermining legal stability; therefore, the retroactive effect of the unconstitutional decision also extends to A.
C: If, before the unconstitutional decision at issue, A had brought an administrative lawsuit seeking revocation of the tax disposition at issue and had already lost with final and conclusive effect, then because the unconstitutional decision at issue constitutes a ground for retrial under Article 75(7) of the Constitutional Court Act, A may petition for retrial.
D: The defect constituting a ground for revocation in the prior disposition, namely the tax disposition at issue, is succeeded to by the subsequent delinquent tax disposition, namely the attachment disposition.
E: If the statutory provision that served as the basis for the imposition of tax is declared unconstitutional, then, because of the binding force of the unconstitutional decision, it is no longer permitted to commence or continue a new delinquent tax collection disposition for the enforcement of the tax claim after the unconstitutional decision. A delinquent tax collection disposition made in violation of the effect of such unconstitutional decision is, by that reason alone, so seriously and objectively manifestly defective as to be void ab initio.
label: E

question: Which of the following statements concerning the rights and duties of public officials is correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: The State Public Officials Act does not prescribe the “principle of statutory determination of working conditions” with respect to public officials’ remuneration, etc., so payment of public officials’ remuneration is possible if it has been included in the national budget.
B: Among the provisions of the State Public Officials Act, the part stating that elementary and secondary school teachers who are education public officials may not participate in the formation of or join “other political organizations” violates the principle of clarity.
C: Unlike military personnel, civilian military employees who are not in the status of State public officials should not be subject to strict restrictions on freedom of political expression, and acts of civilian military employees publicly expressing political opinions also do not need to be strictly restricted.
D: The “collective acts for purposes other than official duties” prohibited by the State Public Officials Act do not refer only to “collective acts that are contrary to the public interest and that have effects such as neglecting the duty of devotion to duty,” but mean all collective acts undertaken by public officials for any purpose other than official duties, based on the mission of public officials as servants of the entire people.
E: Because of a provision of the former Rules on the Payment of Honorary Retirement Allowances, etc. for Judges and Court Officials, which provided that the amount of a judge’s honorary retirement allowance be calculated not only on the basis of the remaining period until mandatory retirement age but also by reflecting the remaining term of office, there is a possibility that a judge may suffer disadvantage as compared with “other career public officials” in whether an honorary retirement allowance is paid and in its amount, etc.; this constitutes arbitrary discrimination.
label: B

question: Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (×) regarding the right to informational self-determination? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a).= The statutory provision that designates a person whose conviction for the offense of indecent assault in a crowded public place has become final as a person subject to registration of personal information, regardless of the gravity of his or her criminal liability, infringes the right to informational self-determination. (b). The statutory provision that requires game business operators to establish a procedure enabling identity verification when a user of a game product registers as a member does not infringe the right to informational self-determination. (c) The statutory provision that requires a person subject to a security surveillance disposition to report the fact of release within 7 days after release from prison, etc., and punishes a violation thereof, does not infringe the right to informational self-determination because the inconvenience to the person subject to the security surveillance disposition is not great and the 7-day reporting period cannot be said to be excessively short. (d) The statutory provision that allows DNA identification information to be entered into and managed in a database until the death of the person subject to collection infringes the right to informational self-determination because it is uniformly applied merely upon the finalization of a conviction for the target offenses, without any consideration of the gravity of the offense, the risk of recidivism, and the like. (e) The statutory provision that requires the public announcement of the violation facts concerning a daycare center that received a suspension of operation, a closure order, or a penalty surcharge because it received subsidies by falsehood or other improper means or misappropriated subsidies does not infringe the right to informational self-determination because it is intended to prevent similar violations by daycare center installers/operators and to ensure the right of guardians of infants and young children to choose a childcare institution.
label: A

question: Which of the following is the correct combination of the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (×) regarding the right to a trial? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) Even if a statute provides that a lawsuit seeking revocation of a disciplinary disposition by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court against a judge shall be tried by the Supreme Court as a single-instance trial, this can be deemed reasonable because it is intended to promote the promptness of adjudication in light of the status of a judge and the special nature of disciplinary proceedings against judges; therefore, it cannot be said that the judge’s right to a trial is thereby infringed. (b) Since seized articles exist for the benefit of the prosecutor who seeks to prove the facts charged, the act of investigative authorities arbitrarily disposing of articles seized in the course of an arrest of a flagrant offender, but without the defendant’s waiver of ownership, cannot be deemed to infringe the defendant’s right to a fair trial. (c) Since extradition proceedings are inherently criminal-procedure in nature, and criminal procedure as a trial procedure naturally includes procedures for challenge to a higher court, a statutory provision that places extradition review under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Seoul High Court and does not recognize a procedure for challenge to the Supreme Court infringes the extraditable person’s right to a trial. (d) Because granting the defendant a right of access to the trial procedure concerning medical treatment and custody is deemed necessary in order to more effectively secure the defendant’s rights, the “right of the defendant himself or herself to request medical treatment and custody” is also included within the scope of protection of the right to a trial.
label: C

question: Which of the following statements concerning freedom of religion is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: The act by the Commander of the Army Training Center of compelling recruits to attend one of the Protestant, Buddhist, Catholic, or Won Buddhist religious events held at the religious facilities within the Army Training Center favors a particular religion and thus violates the principle of separation of religion and state.
B: Since conscientious objection to military service is based on an earnest hope and determination for the peaceful coexistence of humankind, a provision of the ｢Military Service Act｣ that compels performance of military service for conscientious objectors who have not been specially exempted from military service does not restrict the freedom of religion of the relevant religious person, even when applied to a person who refuses military service on the basis of religious belief.
C: The act of the Commissioner of the Statistics Korea, while conducting the face-to-face interview survey of the Population and Housing Census, of requiring respondents through the responsible enumerators to answer the survey items asking whether they have a religion and, if so, what specific religion it is, is one of the survey matters to be used as basic data for statistics and is not intended to impose disadvantages on the ground that one believes in a particular religion or to compel conduct contrary to religious conviction.
D: A statutory provision that also imposes a duty to file a report on the establishment of an elderly care facility operated by a religious organization as part of relief activities and punishes violations thereof does not infringe freedom of religion, because in elderly care facilities of a certain size or larger, the degree of harm from safety accidents or human rights violations may increase, so it is necessary to impose the reporting duty without exception.
E: A statutory provision that, for a person who has been subjected to a disciplinary confinement measure, prohibits attendance at religious rites or religious events, except for religious activities through religious counseling during the period of the disciplinary confinement measure, does not infringe the freedom of religion of the relevant inmate, because such disadvantage cannot be said to outweigh the public interest in maintaining order in detention through compliance with discipline.
label: B

question: Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (×) regarding property rights? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) Article 13(2) of the Constitution provides, “All citizens shall not be deprived of property rights by retroactive legislation ...,” and here retroactive legislation refers only to laws with genuine retroactive effect. (b) An order for culling under the Act on the Prevention of Contagious Animal Diseases should be regarded as exceeding the scope of social restrictions that livestock owners must tolerate, in that it deprives already formed property rights individually and concretely. (c) A provision of the Act on Dam Construction and Assistance to Surrounding Areas, etc. that allows dam use rights to be cancelled or changed cannot be viewed as providing for expropriation, use, or restriction under Article 23(3) of the Constitution, which requires compensation, insofar as it individually and concretely deprives or restricts already formed specific property rights for the public interest; rather, it should be regarded as a provision that both defines the content and limits of dam use rights, which are exclusive rights of use concerning multipurpose dams constructed for public-interest purposes such as adequate water supply and flood prevention, and concretizes the social restrictions on property rights according to public-interest demands. (d) Where the business of a waste recycling processing reporting business operator under the former provisions falls within the category of waste intermediate treatment business under the amended provisions, an existing waste recycling processing reporting business operator who is effectively forced to discontinue business due to the supplementary provisions of the former Waste Management Act, which require obtaining a permit for waste intermediate treatment business under the amended provisions within 1 year from the date of enforcement of the Act in order to continue business, may receive compensation under Article 23(3) of the Constitution on the ground of infringement of property rights.
label: D

question: Which of the following is the correct combination of the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (×) regarding the Warrant Requirement? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) A warrant issued ex officio by a court has the character of a warrant of authorization, but an arrest warrant issued upon the request of an investigative agency has the character of a warrant of command. (b) A statutory provision that permits the relevant administrative authority, when it discovers a game product that has not been subjected to rating classification or a game product with content different from that of a game product that has received rating classification, to have the relevant public official collect and dispose of it, is intended to address an urgent situation; since its inevitability and legitimacy are sufficiently recognized, even if collection without a warrant is permitted, it cannot be regarded as violating the Warrant Requirement. (c) A decision by the Minister of Justice prohibiting the departure from the country of a national whose criminal trial is pending constitutes a compulsory disposition directly involving physical coercive force against the body to which the Warrant Requirement applies. (d) An act by the warden of a prison of requiring an inmate who is a drug offender to provide urine for a drug reaction test constitutes a compulsory disposition against the body and thus violates the Warrant Requirement.
label: A

question: Bar Examination, 13th Session, Public Law Multiple-Choice Question 8. Which of the following is the correct combination of the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (×) regarding the pardon system? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) The President may grant amnesty, commutation of sentence, or restoration of rights as provided by law, and under the Act on the Pardon, etc., when general amnesty, general commutation of sentence, or general restoration of rights is granted, the consent of the National Assembly must be obtained. (b) Under the Act on the Pardon, etc., when the Minister of Justice submits to the President a recommendation for special amnesty, commutation of sentence for a specified person, and restoration of rights, it must undergo review by the Pardon Review Committee, and when the President grants special amnesty, commutation of sentence for a specified person, and restoration of rights, the consent of the National Assembly is not required. (c) Restoration of rights shall not be granted to a person whose execution of sentence has not yet been completed or who has not been exempted from execution. (d) Because an individual convict has no subjective right to demand special amnesty or commutation of sentence, there is no constitutional duty to act or statutory duty on the President, the Minister of Justice, etc. to grant special amnesty to, or commute the sentence of, a convict.
label: D

question: Which of the following explanations concerning the requirements for admissibility of an adjudication on a dispute over authority is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: The chairperson of the Agenda Adjustment Committee under the National Assembly Act does not fall under a state organ that may file an adjudication on a dispute over authority as prescribed by the Constitution and the Constitutional Court Act, and therefore legal capacity as a party in an adjudication on a dispute over authority is not recognized.
B: Under the current legal system, which contains no statutory provision permitting “third-party litigation standing” in an adjudication on a dispute over authority, a petition for adjudication on a dispute over authority filed by National Assembly members alleging that their right of consent was infringed in the conclusion of a contract that would become a burden on the State in addition to the budget is improper for lack of standing as petitioner.
C: A petition for adjudication on a dispute over authority may be filed only when the respondent’s disposition or omission has infringed, or presents a significant risk of infringing, the petitioner’s authority conferred by the Constitution or by law, and here “disposition” means only something of legal significance and must be an act that may specifically affect the petitioner’s legal status.
D: As a requirement for admissibility of a petition for adjudication on a dispute over authority, “omission” does not mean a mere de facto omission, but means failure to perform despite the existence of a constitutional or statutory duty to act.
E: Regardless of whether an act of a state organ constitutes the exercise of its independent power conferred on that state organ by the Constitution and laws, if such act of a state organ is subject to restrictions by another state organ, the possibility that the authority referred to in an adjudication on a dispute over authority is infringed may be recognized.
label: E

question: Which of the following statements concerning directness, an admissibility requirement for a constitutional complaint adjudication, is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: Since statutes, as a general rule, infringe fundamental rights only through concrete enforcement acts as an intermediary, an individual who has suffered an infringement of fundamental rights is, first of all, required, by the nature of a constitutional complaint, to pursue relief for the infringement of fundamental rights through the method of ordinary litigation by targeting that enforcement act.
B: A provision of the Act on the Performance of Duties by Police Officers that prescribes the requirements for the use of water cannon, etc. presupposes a concrete enforcement act, namely the police’s water-spraying act at an assembly or demonstration site, and therefore directness of the infringement of fundamental rights is not recognized.
C: A provision of the Enforcement Rule of the Judicial Scriveners Act that provides that the total number of clerical staff for a judicial scrivener shall not exceed 5 does not directly bring about the effect of dismissing clerical staff, and therefore directness of the infringement of fundamental rights is not recognized.
D: A provision of the Prosecutors Disciplinary Act that prescribes the composition of the members of the Prosecutors Disciplinary Committee does not recognize directness of the infringement of fundamental rights because that Act contemplates a separate disciplinary disposition.
E: A provision of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Execution of Sentences and the Treatment of Inmates that grants the prison warden discretion to open correspondence does not recognize directness of the infringement of an inmate’s fundamental rights because it presupposes a concrete enforcement act, such as the prison warden’s act of checking prohibited items.
label: C

question: Among the explanations concerning personal liberty, which of the following are all incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) A statutory provision that allows the reduction or exemption of a sentence for a person who has served all or part of the sentence in a foreign country does not infringe personal liberty because it falls within the scope of the legislator's legislative discretion. (b) Unlike punishment, a security measure is based on the actor's future risk of recidivism, and since whether to pronounce a security measure is determined by assessing the risk of recidivism at the time of trial rather than at the time of the act, even if a certain security measure has a strong penal character and restricts personal liberty to a degree equivalent to deprivation of personal liberty, the principle of non-retroactivity of punishment does not apply. (c) Excluding foreigners detained pursuant to the Immigration Control Act from the scope of detainees who may file a petition for relief under the Habeas Corpus Act deprives them of the opportunity to contest the legality of their detention under the Habeas Corpus Act and thus infringes personal liberty. (d) A statutory provision that states that a person who has received a deportation order may be detained in a detention facility until deportation becomes possible if the person cannot be immediately deported outside the Republic of Korea infringes personal liberty because it emphasizes only administrative convenience and uniformity. (e) The right to meet and communicate with counsel, in light of the constitutional provisions, is a fundamental right concerning personal liberty limited only to suspects or accused persons who have been arrested or detained, and it cannot be said that those provisions derive a right of counsel to meet and communicate with an arrested or detained suspect or accused person.
label: D

question: Among the explanations concerning the Executive Branch, which is correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: The Prime Minister, upon the President’s order, directs and supervises the heads of each central administrative agency, and when an order or disposition by the head of a central administrative agency is recognized as unlawful, he may suspend or revoke it without obtaining the President’s approval.
B: If the Prime Minister is unable to perform his duties due to an accident, the Deputy Prime Minister who concurrently serves as Minister of Education, and then the Deputy Prime Minister who concurrently serves as Minister of Economy and Finance, shall act in his stead in that order; and if both the Prime Minister and the Deputy Prime Ministers are unable to perform their duties due to an accident, then, if the President makes a designation, the State Council member so designated shall act in his stead, and if there is no designation, the State Council member according to the order prescribed in Article 26(1) of the Government Organization Act shall act in his stead.
C: Even if the President did not undergo deliberation by the State Council in the process of deciding to suspend operations of the Kaesong Industrial Complex, it cannot be said that the decision had a defect of violating the procedures prescribed by the Constitution and laws, or that it had a defect of not undergoing procedures necessarily required under the principle of due process.
D: The Constitution establishes the Board of Audit and Inspection under the President in order to conduct audit and inspection of public officials’ duties, etc. The scope of the Board of Audit and Inspection’s authority to inspect duties includes the authority to request disciplinary action from the appointing authority, and illegality is the standard for audit, while impropriety is not the standard.
E: When the President’s term expires or the office becomes vacant, or when the President-elect dies or loses his qualification by judgment or other reasons, a successor shall be elected within a certain period, and the same applies when the President is unable to perform his duties due to an accident.
label: C

question: Which of the following statements regarding legal interest under the Administrative Litigation Act are correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) The competent administrative agency granted A a permit to alter the structure of the lodging business so that guest rooms could be installed on the 4th and 5th floors of a building owned by A, and A person who operates an inn at a distance of about 700 m from there filed an action seeking a declaration of invalidity of the disposition granting A the permit to alter the structure of the lodging business, on the ground of infringement of residential peace and the living environment; in such case, there is a benefit in seeking a declaration of invalidity. (b) B's term of office expired while an action seeking revocation of the dismissal disposition was pending; however, if the dismissal disposition is revoked, and B can claim payment of remuneration for the period from the date of the dismissal disposition until the date of expiration of the term of office, B has legal interest in seeking revocation of the dismissal disposition. (c) Under the statutes concerning the Act on Promotion of Installation of Waste Disposal Facilities and Support for Nearby Areas, etc., where residents living within 2 km from the site boundary line of a waste landfill facility and within 300 m from the site boundary line of a waste incineration facility are required to form a residents' support consultative body and consult on the determination of the surrounding influence area, if C, a local resident within that area, files an action seeking revocation of the disposition determining the surrounding influence area, standing to sue is recognized. (d) D received a business suspension disposition, and although the suspension period has elapsed, the disposition criteria prescribed in the form of Enforcement Rules provide that a punitive administrative disposition previously imposed shall be treated as an aggravating factor and that a future punitive administrative disposition shall be imposed; where such Enforcement Rules have a statutory basis and there is a risk of receiving an aggravated punitive disposition, if an action seeking revocation is filed against the business suspension disposition whose suspension period has already elapsed, there is legal interest in seeking revocation.
label: E

question: "A private individual, A, while serving in the military suffered a fall accident and received treatment from military physician B, but after being medically discharged from the military, while receiving veterans’ compensation benefits pursuant to statutes, alleged that A suffered a disability due to B’s intentional act or gross negligence and filed a claim for damages against the Republic of Korea and B. During the pendency of the above proceedings, A applied for a motion to refer the proviso to Article 2(1) of the State Compensation Act, which limits the right of soldiers, etc. to claim state compensation, for constitutional review. Among the following explanations, which correctly combines what is correct (○) and what is incorrect (×)? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.) (a) A’s application for a motion to refer for constitutional review is subject to mandatory attorney representation because the party is a private person. (b) The judge in charge of the damages claim lawsuit filed by A must refer the provision of the State Compensation Act to the Constitutional Court for constitutional review even where the judge merely has a simple doubt as to its unconstitutionality. (c) If the motion to refer for constitutional review is dismissed, A cannot file an appeal or re-appeal by way of civil proceedings against the dismissal decision, and cannot file a special appeal either. (d) When the motion to refer for constitutional review is dismissed and A intends to file a constitutional complaint, if A lacks the financial ability to nominate an attorney as representative, A may apply to the Constitutional Court for the appointment of court-appointed counsel.
label: A

question: Which of the following statements concerning impeachment trials is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: To recognize the interest in impeachment adjudication, it is necessary for the respondent to retain the relevant public office until the time the impeachment decision is pronounced.
B: Even if the respondent was lawfully impeached while holding public office at the time of the impeachment motion, if the respondent retires from that office during the pendency of the impeachment trial, this constitutes a ground that bars the continuation of the adjudicative proceedings, and therefore a declaration of termination of the adjudicative proceedings must be made in the operative part.
C: The Constitution expressly states the grounds for impeachment as “violation of the Constitution or laws,” and by assigning jurisdiction over impeachment trials to the Constitutional Court, it defines the impeachment procedure not as a political adjudicative procedure but as a normative adjudicative procedure; accordingly, it reveals that the purpose of the impeachment trial procedure is removal “based on legal violations rather than political reasons.”
D: A decision of removal under the impeachment trial procedure deprives a high-ranking public official of the executive branch or the judiciary who is the respondent of public office, and this constitutes a restriction on the right to hold public office.
E: Removal by the Constitutional Court’s impeachment decision does not amount to an unjust deprivation of public office, provided that its requirements and procedures are observed, and it does not undermine the balance under the principle of separation of powers.
label: B

question: Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (×) regarding the electoral system and suffrage? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents..) (a) The provision of the Public Official Election Act that, with respect to an elector who cannot mark the ballot himself or herself due to a physical disability, if the voting assistant is not a family member, permits assistance in voting only when accompanied by two voting assistants, sets forth an exception to the principle of secret ballot, but does not infringe the right to vote because it maintains the secrecy of the vote by preventing, through criminal punishment, the voting assistant from infringing the secrecy of the elector's vote. (b) The former provision of the Public Official Election Act that criminally punishes campaign activities conducted individually face-to-face and orally before the campaign period infringes the freedom of political expression. (c) The provision of the Public Official Election Act that provides for a single-member district plurality system, under which a person who obtains the majority of valid votes in the relevant National Assembly constituency in an election for a member of the National Assembly from a constituency is determined as the elected person, excludes other electoral systems and therefore infringes the right to equality and the right to vote. (d) In an election for the head of a local government, since the opportunity to attend the interviews and debates that the Election Broadcasting Debate Commission at each level is required to hold must be afforded equally to all candidates, the provision of the Public Official Election Act that restricts eligibility for invitation infringes the right to equality in relation to the principle of equal opportunity for candidates' campaign activities.
label: A

question: Which of the following statements regarding the nationality of the Republic of Korea is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: A person who becomes a dual national before reaching 20 years of age shall choose one nationality pursuant to the procedures prescribed by the Nationality Act by the time he or she reaches 22 years of age, and a person who becomes a dual national after reaching 20 years of age shall choose one nationality within 2 years from that time. However, this shall not include a dual national who, pursuant to the same Act, has pledged to the Minister of Justice that he or she will not exercise a foreign nationality in the Republic of Korea.
B: A national of the Republic of Korea who acquires the nationality of the spouse by marriage to a foreigner shall, within 6 months from the time of acquiring such foreign nationality, notify the Minister of Justice that he or she does not intend to retain Korean nationality, and if the Minister of Justice recognizes this, he or she shall lose Korean nationality from the time of such notification.
C: The provision of the Nationality Act stating, “The Minister of Justice may revoke the permission or determination granted to a person who has obtained permission for naturalization, permission for restoration of nationality, permission to renounce nationality, or a determination of retention of nationality by false or other wrongful means,” does not infringe the freedom of residence and movement or the right to pursue happiness insofar as it concerns revocation of permission for restoration of nationality.
D: A dual national shall choose one nationality within 3 months from the time he or she is incorporated into the military service preparatory status pursuant to Article 8 of the Military Service Act, and a provision of the Nationality Act that prohibits filing a report of loss of nationality after that period and before the military service obligation has been extinguished infringes the freedom to renounce nationality.
E: In a provision of the Nationality Act, the requirement that a person be “of upright conduct” means being endowed with character and conduct such that there is no impediment to accepting a naturalization applicant as a new member of the Republic of Korea, and thus does not violate the principle of clarity.
label: B

question: Which of the following statements concerning the constitutional principle of responsibility is NOT correct? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: A provision of the former Ship Safety Act that stipulates that, where a captain employed by a shipowner commits a criminal act in relation to the shipowner’s business, the same fine shall also be imposed on the shipowner violates the principle of responsibility, because it imposes criminal punishment on the shipowner merely on the ground that the captain employed by the shipowner committed a criminal act in relation to his duties, without at all providing for the shipowner’s independent responsibility for the consequences of the act committed by the captain.
B: A provision of the Labor Standards Act that, where a construction subcontractor who has not registered as a construction business fails to pay wages to workers, imposes on the immediate upper-tier contractor an obligation to pay wages jointly and severally with the subcontractor and punishes the immediate upper-tier contractor if it fails to perform that obligation, cannot be regarded as violating the principle of self-responsibility.
C: A provision of the former Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party that requires the head of each central administrative agency to restrict the qualification for participation in bidding, within the extent prescribed by Presidential Decree and not exceeding 2 years, for a person, etc. who is likely to undermine the fair execution of competition or the proper performance of a contract does not violate the principle of self-responsibility, because it enables the disqualified contractor to escape the sanction disposition by proving, among other things, that the act serving as the cause of the sanction disposition cannot be attributed to him or her.
D: A provision of the National Health Insurance Act that allows the National Health Insurance Service to collect all or part of an amount equivalent to the benefit costs from a medical care institution that has received insurance benefit costs by fraud or other wrongful means does not run counter to the principle of responsibility, because, even if the medical care institution has fulfilled its duty of care to manage and supervise its employees, the insurance benefit costs have once accrued to the medical care institution, and once that medical care institution has received insurance benefit costs by fraud or other wrongful means, it has an obligation to return unjust enrichment.
E: A provision of the Act on the Management of Mountainous Districts that directly punishes a corporation, together with employees, etc., for certain criminal acts committed by employees, etc. employed by the corporation cannot readily be regarded as violating the principle of responsibility because it punishes the corporation’s negligence in failing to fulfill its own duty of direction and supervision.
label: E

question: Which of the following statements concerning the principle prohibiting retroactive legislation is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, follow the precedents.)
A: A provision of the former Special Act on the Improvement of Air Quality in the Seoul Metropolitan Area, which requires an owner operating a specific diesel vehicle equipped with an emission reduction device to return the emission reduction device when, after the amendment of the provision, a separate factual requirement of "cancellation of vehicle registration for scrapping or export, etc." is satisfied, constitutes non-genuine retroactive legislation.
B: A provision of the Commercial Building Lease Protection Act that extended the period for a commercial building tenant to exercise the right to demand contract renewal from 5 years to 10 years, and a supplementary provision of the same Act providing that this amended provision applies to leases renewed after the enforcement of the amended Act even if the lease was concluded before the enforcement of the amended Act, constitute genuine retroactive legislation and violate the principle prohibiting retroactive legislation.
C: A supplementary provision of the former Government Employees Pension Act that provides that, except in cases of "negligence unrelated to official duties" and "negligence while following a lawful official order of a superior officer to whom the official belongs," if a public official is sentenced during service to imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment for a cause arising during service, retirement benefits, etc. shall be reduced, and that the amended provision applies from the following year, does not constitute genuine retroactive legislation.
